entities.summary:
The COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia began on March 6, 2020, and was a significant public health crisis in the country's history. The pandemic led to a national response, with the government implementing various measures to contain the spread of the virus, including lockdowns, social distancing, and mask mandates. The pandemic had a profound impact on the country's economy, with many businesses forced to close and millions of people losing their jobs. The pandemic also had a devastating effect on the country's healthcare system, with hospitals overwhelmed and medical staff working tirelessly to care for the sick.

The pandemic was caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which was first detected in Wuhan, China in December 2019. The virus spread rapidly around the world, infecting millions of people and causing widespread illness and death. The pandemic was a major global health crisis, with the World Health Organization (WHO) declaring it a pandemic in March 2020.

The legacy of the pandemic in Colombia includes a renewed focus on public health and a stronger healthcare system. The pandemic also led to a greater awareness of the importance of preparedness and response to health crises.
